description:
should_gc's floor is young_bytes >= max(live_baseline, SIZE_TABLE[0]/2) = 512 B once live_baseline collapses; the major trigger's reference uses the same 512 B (next_generation). No measurement justifies it: inherited tip geometry (fz-gl6 d2ecc9d48, fz-sc8.184.3 888ec526f). Measured (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/notes.md round 2): trickle collects at 8,496 of 8,496 yields, each copying <256 B; a parent/child ping-pong collects at ~78% of 320k round trips and runs majors at tiny heaps. A near-empty collection costs ~35-40k instructions (msg ~71k). Floor 4/16/64 KiB: msg instructions -27%/-43%/-55%, enum/dist/maps mean RSS unchanged at 4-16 KiB; spin/trickle instructions only -0.4..-1.2%. Failed the pre-registered rule (2 of 3 near-empty workloads) because only msg gains. Next: an experiment across several message-passing workloads (fan-in, ring, request/reply with payloads) with the rule fixed first; derive the floor from what a collection costs vs the bytes it can reclaim rather than picking a constant.

Correction to the close reason: the 39% gift_copy / 18% collection split comes from a profile of a debug-runtime build of msg. It has not been re-measured on release. Explainer: https://claude.ai/artifact/EAx7onN67JBAT7LeRTr72X

comments.text: Reopened. Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (GC session, BEAM comparison on bench, fz develop vs BEAM 28.3). Collections per run fz vs BEAM: ring 75,009 vs 3; msg 106,062 vs 5,223; trickle 4,814 vs 2,218. GC time: ring 11.1 ms vs 0.0; msg 16.9 ms vs 0.9. BEAM collects only when the young heap is full (minimum 233 words, ~1.9 KB) and never because a process parked; fz collects at a park once 512 B of young data has accumulated. Plan: re-test across ring, msg, fanin, reqrep and trickle with the rule fixed before running; memory judged in in-use bytes (fz-9x7.16).

Round 3 (2026-11-17, develop 458eb43eb; data scratchpad/7r3/, analysis.txt). Rule FAILS for every arm on clause 1: only msg and ring pass (collections -50%, instructions -2%); reqrep (best -11% collections, -0.9% instr), fanin (unchanged) and trickle (-73% collections at YM16 but -1.35% instr) do not. Y2 passes clauses 2-4 (msg 0.960, ring 0.849 instructions; memory within bounds). Higher floors fail memory: ring 16 processes x floor (Y16 peak 2.8x, YM16 15.5x); raising the major floor lets promoted data pile up in old (trickle YM16 peak 751 KB vs 29.7 KB). F, the fixed cost of a near-empty collection, is now ~1,850 (ring) to ~3,150 (trickle) instructions, 10-20x below round 2's 35-40k; a 64 MiB floor saves only ~1% of trickle. Majors remain the gap to BEAM: msg Y16 0/1942 vs BEAM 8079/11; reqrep's server stays a major at nearly every park. Measurement caveat: instructions retired varied 0.6-1.9% between identical runs on this machine (load average ~55; spin 0.7%), above the 0.35% guard; close guards need the bench machine. Stays open.

Base caveat: the 2026-11-17 measurements ran on develop 458eb43eb, after #720 (fz-9x7.31), where release cheney_scan calls forward_heap_value out of line at its 8 trace sites (distiller +1.91% instructions per the Make Distiller Fast session's bisect; fix under test by the Bugs and Cleanup session). Collection-heavy ratios (and round 3's per-collection cost F) should be re-read once the inlining is restored.
User ruling 2026-11-18: round 3 closes as failed by rule; the ticket stays open and its floor is re-tested after fz-9x7.11 (which gets a fresh look).

User ruling 2026-11-18 (relayed by GC): round 3 closes as failed by rule; ticket stays open; its floor is re-tested after fz-9x7.11 (now blocks this). Pre-registered guards are judged on the bench machine from now on (local instruction counts vary 0.6-1.9% between identical runs at load ~55).

title: A process with a nearly empty young generation does not collect at every park or yield
